name: Wistia MCP Server
tagline: Official Wistia remote MCP: upload, trim, caption, dub, publish, and read the analytics.
description: Wistia's official hosted MCP puts a whole video library behind an agent: upload or import media, trim and swap versions, order captions, translations, dubs and extended audio descriptions, drive the Remix AI editor, organise folders, tags and channels, then read engagement and visitor analytics back out. For a film team it is the delivery-and-measurement end — festival reels, behind-the-scenes cuts, press kits and webinars hosted somewhere you can see who actually watched, and for how long. A ?toolsets= query parameter on the endpoint narrows the surface to media, analytics, captions, remix or nine other groups instead of exposing everything at once.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add --transport http wistia https://api.wistia.com/mcp/api

auth.key_url: Browser OAuth against a Wistia account, or an access token sent as an Authorization: Bearer header; either way the seat must be Owner or Manager

caveats: Role-gated: only Owners and Managers can connect an agent, so a shared editor seat gets nothing.
By default the endpoint exposes every tool it has, so pin ?toolsets=media,analytics or similar.
The write surface is a live public library; archive, swap, trim and channel publishing are all reachable and some are irreversible.
Marketing and B2B hosting, not screener or festival delivery: no DCP and no watermarked screener workflow.
notes: Launched 2026-07-22 and free to use on any plan, including the $0 tier (25 GB, one seat) — but role-gated: only Owners and Managers can connect an agent, so a shared editor seat gets nothing. Wistia does not publish individual tool names, only the twelve toolsets, and by default the endpoint exposes every tool it has; pin ?toolsets=media,analytics or similar unless you want the agent paging through the full API. The write surface is a live public library — archive, swap, trim, bulk update and channel publishing are all reachable and some are irreversible, so gate them yourself. Remix and dubbing spend an AI credit balance that the account toolset reports. There is no source repo and the docs are the only reference, and Wistia's own guidance is to ask the agent what it can do because the surface is still expanding. Scope check: this is marketing and B2B video hosting, not a screener or festival delivery platform — no DCP, no watermarked screener workflow. For those, see the Frame.io and Vimeo entries. Re-checked 7 Oct 2026: endpoint, Claude Code command, OAuth-or-token auth, Owner/Manager restriction and the twelve toolsets all unchanged in the docs.

name: Canva MCP
tagline: Official Canva remote MCP for campaign designs, thumbnails, decks, exports, and comments.
description: Canva's official remote MCP connects agents to editable design workflows: generate and edit designs, search libraries, manage assets and brand materials, export in delivery formats, resize for channels, and handle comments. For film teams it is the campaign and pitch-collateral bench: YouTube thumbnails, posters, social cutdowns, pitch decks, review decks, and branded variants around the actual film.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add --transport http canva https://mcp.canva.com/mcp

auth.key_url: Canva OAuth; Client ID Metadata Documents (CIMD) is Canva's recommended method, and custom clients may need redirect URI allowlist approval

caveats: Plan gates: nine tools (autofill, brand templates, resize) are Pro and above; Free gets standard-quality exports and only a resize trial.
Per-tool limits run 10 to 100 requests a minute under a 300/min per-user cap shared across all your MCP clients.
Custom OAuth clients may need redirect-URI allowlisting; CIMD is Canva's recommended auth method.
Editing is a four-call transaction flow (start, perform, commit, cancel), easy to miss if you only know generate-and-export.
notes: Re-checked 19 Nov 2026: endpoint https://mcp.canva.com/mcp still returns 401 unauthenticated, so it is alive and OAuth-gated. The surface has grown. The published tools table now lists 46 tools, up from 33 at our 29 Sep check. New since then: image tools (generate-image, remove-background, separate-image-layers), brand-template authoring (create-brand-template-draft, publish-brand-template), plus copy-design, merge-designs, create-design and get-design-dataset. For a film team, layer separation and background removal on key art cover poster and thumbnail prep that used to need a second tool. The four-call editing transaction (start / perform-operations / commit / cancel) is still the part agents miss if they only know generate-and-export. Plan gates: nine tools are Pro and above: the three autofill/dataset tools, five brand-template tools and resize-design (Free gets a limited resize trial). That means data-driven variants, one poster template filled with many cast or territory versions, need at least a Pro seat. Everything else is on all plans. Per-tool limits run 10 to 100 requests a minute (generate-image is the tightest at 10), under a server-wide cap of 300 a minute per user shared across all of that user's MCP clients. Export quality depends on plan: Free gets standard quality, and designs with premium elements can fail with license_required. Canva documents the endpoint rather than a per-client command. CIMD is its recommended auth method, and custom OAuth clients may need redirect-URI allowlisting.

name: Mux MCP Server
tagline: Official Mux MCP: upload, manage, and analyze video via API or hosted remote server.
description: The official MCP server for the full Mux Video + Mux Data platform: upload videos, create and manage assets and live streams, mint playback IDs, manage webhooks, and query video performance analytics. Available both as a hosted remote at mcp.mux.com (OAuth, pick your environment) and as the @mux/mcp npm package — the strongest official offering in video infrastructure. Its two tools are a docs search (search_docs) and a sandboxed TypeScript executor over the Mux SDK, so the whole API surface is reachable without hundreds of tool definitions.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add --transport http mux https://mcp.mux.com

auth.key_url: Remote: OAuth via dashboard.mux.com. Local: MUX_TOKEN_ID + MUX_TOKEN_SECRET from dashboard.mux.com → Settings → Access Tokens

caveats: Two tools only: search_docs and execute, which runs TypeScript against the SDK in a sandbox, so you are writing code, not calling named tools.
v16.0 (27 Oct 2026) is breaking: Robots v1 GA is the default, the beta API is now v0, and Data real-time methods are gone. See MIGRATION.md.
npx -y @mux/mcp stopped starting the server before v16.2.0 fixed it on 11 Nov, so keep @latest or pin 16.2.0 or newer.
notes: npm @mux/mcp v16.2.0 (released 2026-11-11), Apache-2.0, source at muxinc/mux-ts under packages/mcp-server, and the repo is still pushed weekly. The two-tool 'Code Mode' design is unchanged: search_docs queries the docs, and execute runs TypeScript against the @mux/ts SDK in an isolated sandbox, which covers the whole API without hundreds of per-endpoint tools. v16.2.0's only MCP change is a fix that makes `npx -y @mux/mcp` run the server again, plus bumped vulnerable MCP dependencies. If an older pinned version exits on start, that is why. v16.0 (2026-10-27) is the second breaking release in two months. Robots v1 GA became the default, the Robots beta API moved to v0, and the deprecated Data real-time methods and global_value were removed. v16.1 added transcript moderation to Robots and a skipped-track field on video. Code written against v15 needs MIGRATION.md, as v14 code did for the v15 rename (@mux/mux-node to @mux/ts). Deno: local execute now installs Deno itself through an optional npm dependency. Set DENO_PATH to Deno 2.9+ only where that cannot install (blocked downloads, --omit=optional, Alpine), and always for the .mcpb desktop bundle, which never includes it. Set --code-execution-mode=remote to send code to your own sandbox service instead. The hosted remote at mcp.mux.com uses OAuth and falls back to Basic auth (base64 token ID:secret in the Authorization header) for clients without OAuth.

name: yutu (YouTube MCP + CLI)
tagline: Automate your whole YouTube channel — including real video uploads — via OAuth.
description: A Go-based CLI, MCP server, and agent toolkit for YouTube that automates the full workflow: uploading videos, editing metadata, managing playlists, comments, captions, and thumbnails. Still the only well-maintained MCP option that does real YouTube uploads via OAuth — Google ships no official YouTube MCP as of November 2026.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add -e YUTU_CREDENTIAL=/absolute/path/to/client_secret.json -e YUTU_CACHE_TOKEN=/absolute/path/to/youtube.token.json yutu -- yutu mcp

auth.key_url: Google Cloud Console: enable YouTube Data API v3, create a Desktop-app OAuth client, save client_secret.json, then run yutu auth --credential client_secret.json once

caveats: Uploads have their own bucket of 100 videos.insert calls a day; the rest of the API shares the default 10k units.
Unverified API projects can only upload private videos until Google audits them.
You must create a Desktop-app OAuth client in Google Cloud Console and run yutu auth once before yutu mcp works.
v0.11 changed behaviour: OAuth is mandatory for HTTP mode, MCP output defaults to JSON, and destructive tools now ask for confirmation.
notes: 729 stars, Apache-2.0, pushed 2026-11-20. v0.11.1 (2026-11-15) is the current stable release on npm (@eat-pray-ai/yutu), with Homebrew and winget also listed. v0.11.0 (2026-10-02) promoted the September prerelease to stable, and it changes things you will notice. OAuth is mandatory for HTTP mode, MCP output defaults to compact JSON, destructive MCP tools sit behind a confirmation gate, and upload tools refuse sensitive files. The four agents are merged into a single 'Miffy' agent that accepts OpenAI-compatible providers as well as Gemini. v0.11.1 adds `yutu mcp setup --agents claude,...`, which writes the MCP config for the chosen agents with absolute credential and token paths. The claude mcp add command here does the same thing by hand. It also renamed the bundled skill to youtube-automation and hardened the OAuth callback. There are Docker images on Docker Hub and GHCR. Install first (brew install yutu), then authenticate, then run yutu mcp over stdio. Quota has changed in your favour. Google's quota page now gives videos.insert and search.list their own buckets of 100 calls a day at 1 unit each. Everything else shares the default 10,000 units, so the old 1,600-unit upload cost and the six-a-day ceiling no longer apply. Unverified API projects can still only upload private videos until Google audits them. Lighter upload-only alternative: anwerj/youtube-uploader-mcp.

name: YouTube MCP Server (data)
tagline: Token-optimized YouTube Data API server for video, channel, and trend analytics.
description: A high-efficiency MCP server returning structured, token-minimized data from the YouTube Data API v3 (claims up to 87% token reduction vs raw API). Covers video details, search, transcripts, channel statistics, trending, and outlier-channel discovery — the research side of distribution: study what works before you publish.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add youtube -e YOUTUBE_API_KEY=YOUR_KEY -- npx -y @kirbah/mcp-youtube

auth.key_url: Google Cloud Console → enable YouTube Data API v3 → Credentials → API key. Transcript-only use runs with no key at all.

caveats: Read only: no upload, so pair it with yutu.
Quota: searchVideos costs 100 units per call against a 10k a day default.
Transcripts scrape YouTube's timedtext endpoint, a ToS gray area that breaks when YouTube changes it.
MongoDB is required for findConsistentOutlierChannels and recommended for caching; Node 22+.
notes: MIT, npm v1.1.14 released 2026-09-11; that release raised the floor to Node 22+, and everything since has been Dependabot bumps (repo pushed 2026-10-01), so it is maintained rather than developed. Still only 29 stars. Read-only: no upload, so pair it with yutu. Quota reality: searchVideos costs 100 units per call and getChannelTopVideos 101 against a 10k/day default, and getVideoComments is 1 unit plus another per top-level comment once you ask for replies. The 'zero API cost' transcripts do not use the Data API at all — they go through youtube-transcript-plus, which scrapes YouTube's timedtext endpoint, so treat transcript pulls as a ToS gray area and expect them to break when YouTube changes it. MongoDB is less optional than it looks: MDB_MCP_CONNECTION_STRING is required for findConsistentOutlierChannels and the README recommends it for caching everything else. Higher-profile alternative: ZubeidHendricks/youtube-mcp-server (577 stars, but no push since 2026-08-08, multi-key quota fallback).

name: Vimeo MCP Server
tagline: Official Vimeo remote MCP: library search, analytics, retention, and metadata editing.
description: Vimeo's official remote MCP server, now in public beta, connects an agent to your Vimeo library over OAuth. It searches videos across accounts and teams, reads transcripts, chapters, comments and text tracks, pulls performance metrics including geographic data and viewer retention, edits metadata and privacy, manages showcases, and can even create editing sessions and render videos programmatically. For a delivery pipeline it is the honest post-publish feedback loop: what actually held an audience, shot by shot.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add --transport http vimeo https://mcp.vimeo.com/mcp

auth.key_url: OAuth against your Vimeo account; the server advertises https://mcp.vimeo.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource and no token is configured by hand

caveats: Public beta, subject to change without notice, and tool names are unpublished because the docs page is a client-rendered SPA.
Read the six OAuth scopes before you consent: the write surface is genuine, and the scopes decide how much of your library an agent can change.
Vimeo recommends Pro or above because API rate limits scale with plan.
notes: Public beta as of the current docs, upgraded from the private beta announced at REFRAME in Oct 2025 — Vimeo says all of it is subject to change without notice. Endpoint is https://mcp.vimeo.com/mcp; https://mcp.vimeo.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource still answers (re-checked 2026-10-01), names mcp.vimeo.com as its own authorization server, accepts the bearer in the header only, and advertises six scopes — public, private, stats, upload, edit, create. Read that list before you consent: the write surface is genuine, and the scopes you grant decide how much of your library an agent can change. ChatGPT clients use https://mcp.vimeo.com/sse instead, same tools. Destructive actions such as deleting videos are deliberately excluded. Vimeo recommends Pro or above because API rate limits scale with plan, so expect a thin experience on free. The docs page is still a client-rendered SPA and invisible to crawlers (re-checked 2026-10-01), so tool names remain unpublished.

name: Frame.io MCP (community)
tagline: 74 tools over the Frame.io V4 API — comments, shares, version stacks, uploads.
description: A local stdio MCP server for the Frame.io v4 API, built on FastMCP over Adobe's official Python SDK: browse workspaces and projects, upload and download footage, leave timecode-accurate review comments, create client share links, manage version stacks, apply custom metadata in bulk, and manage webhooks. Adobe now runs its own hosted server, listed as `frameio-official`, so this one matters mainly as a self-hosted, self-credentialed alternative.

install.stdio_command: uvx frameio-mcp serve (after a one-time uvx frameio-mcp login --client-id YOUR_ADOBE_SPA_CLIENT_ID)

auth.key_url: https://developer.adobe.com/console — add the Frame.io API and an OAuth Single Page App credential with redirect URI https://localhost:8723/callback; tokens land in ~/.frameio-mcp/tokens.json

caveats: Use frameio-official instead unless you are on a Frame.io Legacy account, and this v4-based server has not been shown to work for those either.
Effectively unmaintained: PyPI 0.1.0 is the only release, and the source repo was rewritten into a Workers server with no public endpoint.
Needs Python 3.13+ and your own Adobe OAuth SPA credential before it does anything.
notes: The Claude Code plugin route is dead. github.com/bowlofarugula/frameio-plugins still 404s (rechecked 2026-11-20), so the old '/plugin marketplace add' command cannot work and claude_code is null. PyPI frameio-mcp 0.1.0 (uploaded 2026-06-04, not yanked) is still the only release as of 20 Nov 2026. A uvx frameio-mcp --help and status run on 2026-08-11 installed clean. It needs Python 3.13+, and you must register your own Adobe OAuth SPA credential before it does anything. Its stated source repo has since been rewritten into a remote Cloudflare Workers server that you would have to deploy yourself. That repo still has 0 stars and has not been pushed since 2026-06-13 (checked 20 Nov 2026), and its /authorize fails closed behind a redirect-URI allowlist, so there is no public endpoint. This is effectively unmaintained: treat it as a working snapshot, not a project. Use `frameio-official` instead unless you are on a Frame.io Legacy account. Adobe's own server went to public beta on 2026-10-07 with a documented hosted endpoint and Adobe ID OAuth, which removes the reason this entry existed. Legacy accounts are the one gap left: the official server does not support them. This server is built on the v4 API, so it has not been shown to work for them either.

name: Frame.io MCP
tagline: Adobe's hosted Frame.io MCP: review comments, shares, version stacks, uploads, and metadata.
description: Frame.io's official remote MCP server puts the review-and-approval layer of a production in front of an agent: search assets across workspaces, read and write review comments, build version stacks, upload media, edit metadata fields, and manage share links, reviewers, and project members. Adobe says it adds nothing the V4 API cannot already do. What it adds is the ability to chain those calls from a prompt. For a film pipeline, that means turning a round of client notes into a task list, or stacking the new cut on the old one and sending the share link, without anyone opening the browser.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add --transport http frameio https://mcp.frame.io/v1/mcp

auth.key_url: OAuth through Adobe IMS — sign in with the Adobe ID linked to your Frame.io account

caveats: Public beta since 7 Oct 2026, so expect churn, and check that you are on the /v1/mcp URL.
Frame.io Legacy accounts are not supported at all.
delete_resources permanently deletes everything except files and folders, so approve each write or delete call.
Tools run with your own permissions, so uploads need Contributor access, and Adobe Managed Accounts can land in the wrong organization.
notes: Public beta as of 7 Oct 2026, per Adobe staff on the forum thread that announced a private beta on 29 Jul. Self-serve now, with no onboarding call, but expect beta churn. Anyone who configured it before 7 Oct should check they are on the /v1/mcp URL. Frame.io Legacy accounts are not supported at all. Adobe Managed Accounts can land in the wrong organization if a stale Adobe session is reused; the docs give a fix. Tools run with your own permissions, so uploads need Contributor access. The write surface is real: `delete_resources` permanently deletes everything except files and folders, which `restore_assets` can bring back. Adobe recommends approving each write or delete call, which is the correct default in front of a client's review project. Adobe's docs give click-through steps for Claude Desktop, ChatGPT, Cursor, VS Code and Copilot CLI, but not a Claude Code command. The command above is the standard remote-HTTP form against the documented URL, and the endpoint's OAuth discovery document answers (checked 10 Oct 2026). There is no source repo, and the docs do not cover MCP-specific pricing; usage counts against your Frame.io plan. Supersedes the community `frameio` entry for every account except Legacy ones.

name: Autoposting
tagline: Social publishing and scheduling for YouTube and other channels, with clip jobs that cut long footage into shorts.
description: Autoposting's hosted server covers the last mile after the cut: connect brand accounts, create and schedule posts, publish to YouTube, Instagram, X, LinkedIn and Threads, and run clip jobs that turn a long video into social cutdowns with captions. Tools are filtered by the OAuth scopes the user grants and carry read-only and destructive annotations, so a client can gate the publish calls. It is a social media operations tool, not an editor.

install.claude_code: claude mcp add --transport http autoposting https://app.autoposting.ai/mcp

auth.key_url: https://autoposting.ai (OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration for the hosted server; the stdio CLI uses an API key)

caveats: Requires a paid Autoposting account plus connected social accounts; the open-source CLI does not make the service free.
Only a sliver of the surface is about film (YouTube publishing, scheduling and the clip renderer); the rest is social media management.
The hosted catalogue differs from the local CLI one, so trust tools/list over either count.
notes: Checked 10 Oct 2026: the hosted endpoint completes initialize (autoposting-mcp 1.0.0) and refuses tools/list without a bearer token, the official MCP Registry lists ai.autoposting/autoposting, and npm @autoposting.ai/cli is at 0.5.5 (MIT, updated 7 Oct 2026). The docs say 68 tools, the README says 69, and the hosted catalogue differs from the local CLI one, so trust tools/list over either. Only a sliver of the surface is about film: YouTube publishing, scheduling and the clip renderer. The rest is social media management (knowledge bases, AI-rewritten posts, carousels). Requires a paid Autoposting account plus connected social accounts; the open-source CLI does not make the service free. For plain YouTube upload without the platform compare youtube-yutu.

name: Repostit
tagline: Hosted OAuth MCP for Repostit's social cross-poster: repost workflows, scheduled posts, publishing and delivery checks.
description: Repostit's connector lets an agent check which social accounts are connected, set up standing repost workflows (every new TikTok to YouTube Shorts, say), create and schedule a one-off post (a 'Brief'), publish it, and confirm delivery per platform. For a film team it handles the cutdown-and-trailer push across TikTok, Instagram, YouTube, X, Threads, LinkedIn and Pinterest once the edit is locked. It is a social cross-posting tool, not a festival or distributor delivery pipeline.

auth.key_url: Browser OAuth (dynamic client registration) against a Repostit account from https://repostit.io, with social accounts already connected there

pricing_note: 14-day trial (10 posts, 3 workflows, no card), then $5/mo for 10 video posts or unlimited-post plans from about $10 to $14/mo.
caveats: The endpoint is a bare Google Cloud Run URL from Repostit's connector page; repostit.io/mcp, the address in the submission, does not serve MCP.
Built for reposting: sources are TikTok, Instagram, Facebook, Pinterest, X or Dropbox, so finished masters go through Dropbox first.
No tool names published and no public repo; the OAuth scopes include publish:write, so gate the publish calls in your client.
notes: Checked 7 Nov 2026: the Cloud Run endpoint answers initialize with 401 Bearer realm="Repostit" and publishes OAuth protected-resource metadata with scopes connections:read, workflows:write, briefs:write, publish:write and status:read. We have no account, so tools/list and tool names are unverified, and the vendor documents actions rather than tool names. The URL is the one on Repostit's own connector page (app.repostit.io/claude-connector.html) and in the official MCP Registry (io.github.hax98/repostit, 2026.10.23, under a staff member's GitHub namespace rather than a repostit domain namespace). repostit.io/mcp returns 404/405, and the user docs only say to find Repostit in Claude's or ChatGPT's connector list, which we did not confirm; if Repostit moves the service, the raw run.app address will break without warning. Platforms per the vendor docs: post from TikTok, Instagram, Facebook, Pinterest, X or Dropbox; publish to TikTok, Instagram, Facebook, YouTube, Pinterest, LinkedIn, X, Threads, Google Drive or Dropbox. No Vimeo, and no direct upload of a local file through the connector is documented. Money: every plan has a 14-day trial with no card (10 posts counted per destination, 1 account per platform, 3 workflows); Basic is $5/mo for 10 video posts; Starter, Influencer and Agency show both $10/$20/$99 and $14/$29/$149 a month, apparently annual versus monthly billing, with 1, 5 and 30 accounts per platform. The terms (effective 7 Mar 2025) name Repostit LLC in Newark, Delaware, while the footer says Repostit, Inc. The domain dates to Nov 2024. Closest neighbour is Autoposting, which also cuts clips; Repostit is the narrower, cheaper cross-poster.
